content: Hydralazine works by relaxing blood vessels, which lowers blood pressure. However, when blood vessels are relaxed, the heart may need to work harder to pump blood, potentially increasing the risk of a heart attack. Hydralazine should not be used in individuals with mitral valvular rheumatic heart disease, a condition caused by damage to the mitral valve due to rheumatic fever. Relaxation of blood vessels by hydralazine can increase blood flow to the heart, placing additional strain on the mitral valve and making the heart work harder. Before using hydralazine, it is essential to consult a healthcare provider. Only take hydralazine if it has been prescribed to you, and follow the prescribed dosage. Do not share hydralazine with others, even if they have a similar condition, as it may harm them. Keep hydralazine out of reach of children. Hydralazine may impair alertness or coordination. Avoid driving or engaging in activities requiring alertness until you understand how hydralazine affects you. Inform your healthcare provider about all your health conditions and any medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, or supplements you are taking. This information helps determine if hydralazine is appropriate for you. If you have a history of heart disease, such as coronary artery disease or a previous heart attack, kidney disease, stroke, or rheumatic fever, inform your healthcare provider. Hydralazine may interact with other medications or supplements, so disclose all prescription and over-the-counter drugs you are using. The effects of hydralazine on pregnancy and an unborn baby are not well understood. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your healthcare provider. Hydralazine passes into breast milk, so your provider will advise whether it is safe to use while breastfeeding. There are no known interactions between hydralazine and foods or nonalcoholic drinks. However, it is unclear if alcohol consumption affects hydralazine. Drinking alcohol while taking hydralazine may increase the risk of dizziness. If you or someone else accidentally takes too much hydralazine, seek immediate medical attention, call 911, or contact a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. If you miss a dose of hydralazine, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take only the next scheduled dose. Do not take double or extra doses. Hydralazine should not be used by individuals allergic to hydralazine, Apresoline, or any ingredients in the specific product. Your pharmacist can provide a list of ingredients in the hydralazine product you are using. Hydralazine is contraindicated in individuals with coronary artery disease (CAD), a condition where the arteries supplying blood to the heart muscle are blocked or narrowed. Relaxation of blood vessels by hydralazine in CAD can cause the heart to work harder, increasing the risk of a heart attack. For the most current information about hydralazine and its interactions, consult your healthcare provider or pharmacist.
